newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI approves rights issues by mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI approves rights issues by mutual funds.

text.p: NEW DELHI, Dec 10 - The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Tuesday that its board of directors decided to permit rights issues by mutual funds, subject to conditions.

"It was felt that in the cases of close-ended schemes, rights issues could be permitted, provided the existing unit holders were given repurchase facility at net asset value (NAV) related price," SEBI said in a statement.

"When we heard that Unit Trust of India will have seven (rights) issues, we said, 'What is the investors' interest in this?'" SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told reporters in New Delhi after a meeting of the regulator's board.

News of the proposed rights issues by Unit Trust of India, India's largest mutual fund, evoked criticism that new units issued by mutual funds could lower the net asset value per unit, which reflects the market price of a unit.
